summary: The article explains how real-time data (GPS tracking, sensors, analytics) is making public transportation more efficient, reliable and accessible. It centers on the Metropolitan Transport Network's "OnRoute" app, with commuter and official quotes on benefits, challenges like cost and tech disparities, emergency use during a storm, and data-driven route planning. It concludes that cities will keep investing in such technology toward smart cities.
one_line: Real-time transit data, exemplified by MTN's OnRoute app, improves commuting, accessibility, emergency response and route planning, despite cost and access challenges.
key_facts: On September 4, 2023, the Metropolitan Transport Network (MTN) announced the launch of its "OnRoute" app.
Transportation analyst David Sanders called the OnRoute rollout "a pivotal move" that reduces waiting times and improves satisfaction with public transport.
Commuter Sarah Jennings says buses fitted with GPS transmitters feed data to a central system every few seconds, which predicts arrival times with precision.
Passengers access real-time information via smartphone apps, digital displays at stations, or online platforms.
Jason Martinez, head of customer experience at MTN, says real-time data helps bridge the gap between life's unpredictability and structured transit schedules.
Barry Thompson, CEO of Accessible Transit Now, said knowing if an elevator is out of service or if a bus has wheelchair space can make the difference between a smooth journey and an ordeal.

City Councilor Jennifer Clarke said the city had to invest significantly in both technology and training, and that data reliability is paramount because trust underpins commuters' relationship with transit.
Disparities in tech accessibility across demographics persist, so outreach programs and user-friendly interfaces are vital.
On September 18, 2023, OnRoute was tested during a major storm, giving riders continuous updates on service outages and reroutes.
Joe Baxter, caught in the city during the storm, said the updates were "lifesaving" and helped him get home safely.
On October 10, 2023, MTN announced bus route changes based on six months of accumulated transit data, aimed at reducing congestion and improving reach in underserved areas.
MTN planning director Anne Richmond said clear patterns in the data let MTN tailor services to community needs more effectively than before.
